thread:
maria (Support): Heads-up — customer reports Azure Marketplace line items are ~3.6M tokens but our Redwood dashboard shows ~1.8M for the same billing period. Invoice AZ-INV-9923 / sub-0a1b2c. They want a breakdown and reconciliation asap. :eyes:

sam (Billing): Ack. Can you paste the exact line items from the marketplace invoice (sku ids + quantities)? Also need the billing period start/end they gave.

maria (Support): Paste from customer: `2026-02-01` to `2026-02-28`. Line items snippet they attached: 
```
SKU: azure.redwood.tokens.standard | Qty: 3600000 | Unit price: $0.0005 | Total: $1,800
SKU: azure.redwood.overage | Qty: 0 | Total: $0
```
They said our dashboard export CSV (usage_tokens column) shows 1,842,143 tokens for that period.

sam (Billing): :thinking: If marketplace billed 3.6M but our metering shows ~1.84M, maybe double-counting on their side or we emitted two metering events for some requests. @marketplace-bot do we have any duplicate metering upload events for sub-0a1b2c in Feb?

marketplace-bot: Metering report received for subscription=sub-0a1b2c, report_id=mr-20260215-77, rows=2, timestamp=1766480000. No automatic duplicate detected by ingress dedupe (hash collision check).

aj (Eng): I'll start by checking the ingestion logs and metering pipeline. Can you share the export CSV you used? Also, any chance the customer has multiple subscriptions under the same tenant?

maria (Support): Uploaded CSV from dashboard: 
```
user_id,usage_date,usage_tokens
u-123,2026-02-03,450000
u-123,2026-02-14,1392143
```
Only one subscription listed in their portal view (sub-0a1b2c). They attached invoice screenshot with the 3.6M number.

kevin (SRE): Quick checks I'll run: 1) check metering ingestion topic for duplicate batches 2) verify event timestamps timezone boundary (UTC vs PST) 3) confirm any backfill jobs in Feb.

aj (Eng): Running query against metering datastore to sum tokens for sub-0a1b2c in Feb. Query: 
```
SELECT sum(tokens) FROM metering_events WHERE subscription = 'sub-0a1b2c' AND event_date BETWEEN '2026-02-01' AND '2026-02-28';
```
Result returned: `1842143` tokens (matches dashboard CSV).

aj (Eng): Also checking raw events ingestion stream for duplicate event_ids. Running grep on logs: 
```
grep 'sub-0a1b2c' /var/log/metering/2026-02-*.log | grep -E "report_id|event_id"
```
Found: two metering reports for that sub: `mr-20260215-77` and `mr-20260216-01`. Combined rows look like: 
```
mr-20260215-77, event_id=e-aaa-1, tokens=900000
mr-20260216-01, event_id=e-bbb-2, tokens=2700000
```

sam (Billing): If the marketplace uploaded two distinct reports that sum to 3.6M that's likely the invoice source. Why does our metering only include one set? Did we drop or dedupe one report during ingestion?

kevin (SRE): Looking at ingestion service logs: `ingest-service` applied dedupe window keyed by `event_id` and a 24h idempotency TTL. The two reports have distinct event_ids, so they wouldn't be deduped. However, I see a downstream job that applies a policy: if report contains a `report_type=estimated` flag we classify it differently and don't attribute to final billing. One report had `report_type=estimated` and we ignored it for usage exports — but marketplace invoice apparently billed both.

maria (Support): So marketplace billed both estimated + final? That could explain the mismatch. Is there a way to confirm the marketplace line item came from both report types?

sam (Billing): Yes, need to map invoice SKU rows back to the marketplace report ids. Azure provides `MeteringReportId` in the invoice metadata sometimes. If the customer can share full invoice JSON or billing CSV we can map. @liz (Account) can you ask customer for the invoice CSV export including metadata?

liz (Account): I'll request the full invoice export and ask them to confirm if they saw two separate submissions in their Azure portal. Messaging them now.

aj (Eng): In parallel I'll re-run ingestion audit to surface all reports for that subscription for Feb and whether any had `report_type` flags. Quick audit command used: 
```
SELECT report_id, report_type, sum(tokens) FROM raw_metering WHERE subscription='sub-0a1b2c' AND report_date BETWEEN '2026-02-01' AND '2026-02-28' GROUP BY report_id, report_type;
```
Result: 
```
mr-20260215-77, final, 900000
mr-20260216-01, estimated, 2700000
```

kevin (SRE): That matches earlier. So our dashboard/export only counts `final` reports; marketplace apparently billed estimated as well. Need to confirm whether Azure's billing pipeline includes both if both were submitted.

sam (Billing): If Azure billed both, customer can request marketplace billing adjustment. But we should also flag mismatch for internal ops: either we should surface estimated reports in our billing exports or add note to customers about estimated vs final.

maria (Support): Proposed next steps: 1) liz: get full invoice CSV & any Azure portal screenshots 2) sam: prepare explanation + steps for customer to request Azure adjustment 3) aj/kevin: confirm internal fix (audit alert + add marketplace ingestion flag to exports) 4) follow up with customer in 48h.

liz (Account): Customer replied with attached invoice CSV (they included meterReportId column). I mapped meterReportId -> our report ids and it's the two we found. They're upset; asking for immediate credit.

sam (Billing): Drafting reply: explain difference between 'estimated' vs 'final' metering reports and that Azure billed both because they accepted both uploads. Offer to assist with Azure support ticket. Also propose short-term credit while we investigate.

aj (Eng): For internal prevention: I'll open a ticket to modify our export pipeline to include `report_type` in monthly usage exports and add an anomaly check where sum(estimated)+sum(final) >> sum(final)*1.2 trigger alert. Filing ENG-1428.

kevin (SRE): Also adding ingestion rule: tag marketplace uploads with `marketplace_report_id` and surface duplicates across report_type. Might help.

maria (Support): Thanks team. I'll update the customer with sam's draft and tell them we're opening an Azure billing case + offering temporary credit. Will update thread when they respond. :thumbsup:

liz (Account): FYI I cc'd our partner ops contact at Azure — they acknowledged and will check whether both reports were processed in their billing pipeline.

maria (Support): Customer replied, they opened a support case with Azure and sent case id AZ-CASE-5543. They asked if Redwood can confirm which report they should ask Azure to reverse. I'll attach mapping in the reply.

sam (Billing): Provide mapping snippet to customer: 
```
mr-20260215-77 -> final -> recommend keep
mr-20260216-01 -> estimated -> recommend reverse if Azure billed both
```

maria (Support): Sent mapping. Ticket will remain open until Azure confirms. Closing internal loop: ENG-1428 created, Billing credited $900 to customer as a temporary goodwill credit. I'll update when Azure responds.

aj (Eng): Noted. I'll follow up on ENG-1428 status next week.

kevin (SRE): I'll add a short runbook for support on marketplace mismatches: how to map invoice rows -> report ids and common fixes. Saves time next time.

maria (Support): Thanks everyone. Marking this thread solved for now; re-open if Azure confirms they won't reverse the estimated row. :white_check_mark:
